# File path built from HTTP request data (Java)

`qualor:java/path-traversal` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A01:2025 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/), [A01:2021 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data in a file path (Jakarta Servlet, Spring MVC, Jakarta REST): `new File(...)`, file
streams and readers, `Paths.get`, `Path.of`, `Path.resolve`, the `Files` methods that use such a
path, an upload written under a request-chosen name (`Part.write`, `MultipartFile.transferTo`),
and Spring file resources (`FileSystemResource`, `UrlResource`, resource locations).
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
`Paths.get("/srv/reports", name)` does not keep the result inside `/srv/reports`: a name such as
`../../etc/passwd` climbs out of it, and `resolve()` with an absolute path drops the base
altogether. A client can then read configuration and keys, overwrite files the application trusts,
or delete data.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the requested name becomes part of the path.

```java
package com.example.reports;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Paths;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class ReportController {
    @GetMapping("/reports")
    public byte[] report(@RequestParam String name) throws IOException {
        return Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get("/srv/reports", name));
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** only the file name is kept, so the path stays in the reports directory.

```java
package com.example.reports;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.Paths;
import org.apache.commons.io.FilenameUtils;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class ReportController {
    private static final Path REPORTS = Paths.get("/srv/reports");

    @GetMapping("/reports")
    public byte[] report(@RequestParam String name) throws IOException {
        return Files.readAllBytes(REPORTS.resolve(FilenameUtils.getName(name)));
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep only the file name: `Path.getFileName()` or Commons IO `FilenameUtils.getName()` (and reject
  `.` and `..`).
- Or map the request value to a server-side name, an allow-list entry or a generated name (a UUID
  you stored).
- When a path must be built from several parts, normalise it and check that it still starts with
  the base directory: `base.resolve(name).normalize().startsWith(base)`.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Jakarta Servlet
- Spring MVC
- Jakarta REST (JAX-RS)

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A check after the path is built (`normalize()` and `startsWith(base)`) is not seen: the path is
  reported where it is built from request data. `Paths.get` and `Path.of` are checked themselves,
  so a path built only to take its file name in a later statement is reported.
- A `MultipartFile`'s original file name counts as request data wherever the `MultipartFile` comes
  from.
- A handler parameter without an annotation is not a source (the Jakarta REST entity parameter, a
  Spring MVC simple-type parameter), except a Spring `HttpEntity` or `RequestEntity` (the
  request body and headers); enum, `List` or `Optional` parameters still count as request data.
- One method is analysed at a time and conditions are not evaluated. Allow-list lookups are
  recognised only as `Map.of(...)` of constants and as `valueOf` of an enum declared in the same
  file.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/java/path/path-traversal.java`](../../../rules/java/path/path-traversal.java) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/java/path/path-traversal.yml`](../../../rules/java/path/path-traversal.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
